correctness.rationale: The binomial interpolation converges uniformly because the kth term has valuation at least k−ν₂(k), and agrees with the combinatorial sequence at each positive index. At 0 and 1 its value is 2; at −1 and −2 it is −2 by the geometric and weighted geometric series, so its forward difference vanishes at 0 and −2. Cao–Pan Theorem 2 extends by continuity to the four residue classes. At even x the signs at x and x+1 are opposite, so the forward-difference increment for a shift by 2^α, α≥2, is 2^(α+2) modulo 2^(α+3). Summing an odd number of increments preserves this exact valuation, giving a distance factor of 1/4 on each even class modulo four. Anchoring at 0 or −2 gives ν₂(n)+2 or ν₂(n+2)+2, respectively; the other factor of n(n+2) has valuation one. On odd indices the α=1 congruence makes D_n constant modulo 16 along steps of two, with D_1=4. The two distinct exact-level classes modulo 2^(j−1) give the stated densities; index zero is correctly excluded. Independent exact rational sums of the displayed binomial series through n=64 checked all first-difference valuations through n=63 and residue sets at levels 4–6. The uploaded recurrence checker was inspected, not executed; neither finite check is the all-index proof.
